name: Small Fiber Neuropathy

ethnicAssociations: Fabry disease-associated SFN more common in certain populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Devigili et al. 2008 / Updated Consensus Criteria

criteria.description: Clinical symptoms consistent with small fiber involvement: burning pain, allodynia, thermal sensitivity changes in length-dependent distribution
Reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) on skin punch biopsy below age- and sex-adjusted normative values
Abnormal quantitative sensory testing (QST) for thermal thresholds
Normal nerve conduction studies (large fiber function preserved)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical symptoms plus reduced IENFD on skin biopsy OR abnormal QST, with normal nerve conduction studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Skin punch biopsy with IENFD quantification is the gold standard diagnostic test. Many patients have idiopathic SFN (~50%). Treatable causes include diabetes, Sjogren syndrome, sarcoidosis, Fabry disease, amyloidosis, and sodium channel mutations.

pathognomonic.notes: Often described as 'feet on fire'; length-dependent pattern starting distally
Pain from normally non-painful stimuli such as bedsheets touching feet
Reduced ability to detect warm and cool temperatures

common.notes: Sweating abnormalities, GI dysmotility, orthostatic intolerance

laboratory: ESR, CRP, ANA, SS-A/SS-B antibodies (autoimmune screen)
Vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, folate levels
SCN9A, SCN10A, SCN11A genetic testing for sodium channelopathies
genetic: SCN9A (Nav1.7) gain-of-function mutations in inherited erythromelalgia and SFN
SCN10A (Nav1.8) mutations associated with painful SFN
GLA gene mutations for Fabry disease
TTR gene mutations for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis
other: Skin punch biopsy with intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) quantification - gold standard
Quantitative sensory testing (QST) for thermal detection thresholds
Normal nerve conduction studies and EMG (by definition)

distinguishingFeatures: Fibromyalgia has widespread pain with tender points
Fibromyalgia has normal skin biopsy IENFD (though some overlap)
Fibromyalgia diagnosed clinically without objective nerve fiber loss
CIDP affects large fibers with abnormal NCS
CIDP has demyelinating pattern on electrodiagnostics
Diabetic neuropathy may include large fiber involvement
Diabetes is a cause of SFN, not a differential
HbA1c and glucose tolerance test help identify

redFlags: Non-length-dependent pattern should prompt evaluation for ganglionopathy or Sjogren syndrome
Young patient with SFN should be screened for Fabry disease
Rapid progression or significant autonomic failure suggests amyloidosis
Family history of SFN suggests sodium channelopathy or Fabry disease
Weight loss and autonomic dysfunction raise concern for amyloidosis
SFN in setting of monoclonal gammopathy requires further hematologic workup
references: Devigili G, et al. The diagnostic criteria for small fibre neuropathy: from symptoms to neuropathology. Brain. 2008;131(Pt 7):1912-1925.
Terkelsen AJ, et al. The diagnostic challenge of small fibre neuropathy: clinical presentations, evaluations, and causes. Lancet Neurol. 2017;16(11):934-944.

Themistocleous AC, et al. The Pain in Neuropathy Study (PiNS): a cross-sectional observational study determining the somatosensory phenotype of painful and painless diabetic neuropathy. Pain. 2016;157(5):1132-1145.
